result.narrative: Intel Corporation sits in the Watch band with a score of 20.7, driven entirely by news rather than any payment deterioration. The payment record is pristine at 0 days past due, contributing nothing to the score, while the full 20.7 points come from a single severity-3 news item on a shareholder lawsuit filed after a 29% stock plunge. All other recent coverage in the evidence set is neutral-to-positive, including new 18A/18A-P foundry customers and stock gains, with no overdue payment or payment_review evidence recorded at all. The adjudicator agreed with the score but flagged caveats: the lawsuit article is a bare headline with no body detail on scope or credit relevance, and shareholder suits following a stock drop are a routine, often opportunistic occurrence rather than a direct liquidity signal, so the Watch classification rests on a thin single source rather than corroborated financial distress. The recommended action is to maintain the current limit of 7,000,000 USD unchanged, as the probability of default (0.1072) remains within appetite and expected loss is unaffected before and after. The buyer sits only 0.7 points above the Healthy band threshold, so even modest easing of the news-driven score would lift it back to Healthy, while a move to High Risk would need the score to climb a further 29.3 points, equivalent to payment delinquency reaching 38 days past due.
